/-!
# McKay conjecture

Let $p$ be a prime, $G$ a finite group and $P \leq G$ a Sylow $p$-subgroup. Write
$$\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G) := \{\chi \in \mathrm{Irr}(G) : p \nmid \chi(1)\}$$
for the set of irreducible complex characters of $G$ whose degree is not divisible by $p$.
The McKay conjecture asserts that
$$|\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)| = |\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(N_G(P))|,$$
where $N_G(P)$ is the normalizer of $P$ in $G$.

The conjecture was stated by McKay in 1971 for $p = 2$ and simple groups, and generalised to all
primes by Alperin. A proof for all primes and all finite groups was announced by Cabanes and
Späth in 2023.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *McKay conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McKay_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [M. Cabanes, B. Späth, *The McKay Conjecture on character degrees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20392)
-/

def irrCharsPrimeToDeg (p : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] : Set (G → ℂ) :=
  {χ | ∃ V : FDRep ℂ G, Simple V ∧ V.character = χ ∧ ¬ p ∣ Module.finrank ℂ V}
blocks.docstring:
The set $\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)$ of irreducible complex characters of the group $G$ whose
degree is not divisible by $p$.

A character is the function `G → ℂ` sending `g` to the trace of `ρ g`, and irreducible
representations are the simple objects of `FDRep ℂ G`. The degree of a character is the
dimension of the underlying representation, i.e. $\chi(1)$ (see `FDRep.char_one`). Since
isomorphic representations have the same character, each isomorphism class of irreducible
representations is counted once.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FDRep.character` (a single character), `CategoryTheory.Simple` (irreducibility of one object of `FDRep ℂ G`), `Representation.IsIrreducible` (unbundled representations; would require quantifying over carrier types and does not give a set of characters). Nothing in FormalConjecturesForMathlib concerns characters.
justification.name: McKayConjecture.irrCharsPrimeToDeg
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no definition of the set Irr(G) of irreducible complex characters of a group, nor of Irr_{p'}(G) = {χ ∈ Irr(G) : p ∤ χ(1)}. The definition packages `FDRep.character`, `CategoryTheory.Simple` and `Module.finrank` into the set of p'-degree irreducible characters as functions `G → ℂ`, so that its `ncard` counts isomorphism classes of irreducible representations.

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem exists_eq_apply_one_of_mem_irrCharsPrimeToDeg {p : ℕ} {G : Type} [Group G]
    {χ : G → ℂ} (hχ : χ ∈ irrCharsPrimeToDeg p G) : ∃ n : ℕ, χ 1 = n ∧ ¬ p ∣ n := by
  obtain ⟨V, -, rfl, hV⟩ := hχ
  exact ⟨Module.finrank ℂ V, FDRep.char_one V, hV⟩

blocks.docstring:
**McKay conjecture.** Let $G$ be a finite group, $p$ a prime and $P$ a Sylow $p$-subgroup
of $G$. Then the number of irreducible complex characters of $G$ of degree not divisible by $p$
equals the number of irreducible complex characters of the normalizer $N_G(P)$ of degree not
divisible by $p$:
$$|\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)| = |\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(N_G(P))|.$$

Here isomorphic representations are counted once. Since all Sylow $p$-subgroups are conjugate,
the right-hand side does not depend on the choice of $P$.

claims.decomposer_note: Universally quantified over finite groups G ("group" means finite group), all primes p and any Sylow p-subgroup P; the list entry's wording drops the "degree not divisible by p" restriction on the normalizer side, but the article's Statement section and Cabanes–Späth (MK) make clear both sides count p'-degree irreducible characters, |Irr_{p'}(G)| = |Irr_{p'}(N_G(P))| (isomorphic representations counted once; well-defined since Sylow subgroups are conjugate), and the claim is now a theorem (Cabanes–Späth 2024) despite the 'open' status label.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful content: for every finite group G, prime p and Sylow p-subgroup P, |Irr_{p'}(G)| = |Irr_{p'}(N_G(P))| with the p'-degree restriction on both sides (as in the article's Statement section and Cabanes–Späth Theorem (MK)); the literal list wording without the restriction on the normalizer side is false (S_4, p=2). Irr_{p'} is modeled as the set of character functions G → ℂ of CategoryTheory.Simple objects of FDRep ℂ G with finrank not divisible by p (Mathlib's documented notion of irreducible representation; FDRep has kernels and a faithful finite-limit-preserving forgetful functor, so monos are injective and Simple = irreducible). Counting a set of character functions counts isomorphism classes once; by FDRep.char_orthonormal the set is finite for finite G, so Set.ncard is never degenerate; the trivial group gives 1 = 1; Sylow.nonempty rules out vacuity. c08 chosen as base: cleanest, complete docstrings and references, a proven (not sorried) API lemma for the bespoke definition, Mathlib-idiomatic [Fact p.Prime] and P.normalizer. Only a docstring edit (paragraph break, pointer to FDRep.char_one) was made. c01/c02/c06 are equivalent (c06 adds a sorried API lemma; c02's docstring contains a review-style remark); c03/c05 inline the set without a named definition; c07 uses Cardinal.mk; c04 uses Representation ℂ G (Fin n → ℂ) with IsSimpleModule (also faithful, universe-polymorphic, but less aligned with Mathlib's FDRep.character API).

context:
In mathematics, specifically in the field of group theory, the McKay conjecture is a theorem of equality between two numbers: the number of irreducible complex characters of degree not divisible by a prime number $p$ for a given finite group and the same number for the normalizer in that group of a Sylow $p$ -subgroup. 
It is named after the Canadian mathematician John McKay, who originally stated a limited version of it as a conjecture in 1971, for the special case of $p=2$ and simple groups. The conjecture was later generalized by other mathematicians to a more general conjecture for any prime value of $p$ and more general groups.
In 2023, a proof of the general conjecture was announced by Britta Späth and Marc Cabanes.

decomposition_objections.text: None on content. Minor note: the table's status is 'open' while its own notes (and the Wikipedia article) record that the statement is now a theorem of Cabanes–Späth (2024); I followed the prescribed status with `research open`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# McKay conjecture

Let $p$ be a prime, $G$ a finite group and $P \leq G$ a Sylow $p$-subgroup. Write
$$\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G) := \{\chi \in \mathrm{Irr}(G) : p \nmid \chi(1)\}$$
for the set of irreducible complex characters of $G$ whose degree is not divisible by $p$.
The McKay conjecture asserts that
$$|\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)| = |\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(N_G(P))|,$$
where $N_G(P)$ is the normalizer of $P$ in $G$.

The conjecture was stated by McKay in 1971 for $p = 2$ and simple groups, and generalised to all
primes by Alperin. A proof for all primes and all finite groups was announced by Cabanes and
Späth in 2023.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *McKay conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McKay_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [M. Cabanes, B. Späth, *The McKay Conjecture on character degrees*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20392)

namespace McKayConjecture

open CategoryTheory

/-- The set $\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)$ of irreducible complex characters of the group $G$ whose
degree is not divisible by $p$.

A character is the function `G → ℂ` sending `g` to the trace of `ρ g`, and irreducible
representations are the simple objects of `FDRep ℂ G`. The degree of a character is the
dimension of the underlying representation, i.e. $\chi(1)$ (see `FDRep.char_one`). Since
isomorphic representations have the same character, each isomorphism class of irreducible
representations is counted once. -/
def irrCharsPrimeToDeg (p : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] : Set (G → ℂ) :=
  {χ | ∃ V : FDRep ℂ G, Simple V ∧ V.character = χ ∧ ¬ p ∣ Module.finrank ℂ V}

/-- Every $\chi \in \mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)$ satisfies $\chi(1) = n$ for a natural number $n$ with
$p \nmid n$. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem exists_eq_apply_one_of_mem_irrCharsPrimeToDeg {p : ℕ} {G : Type} [Group G]
    {χ : G → ℂ} (hχ : χ ∈ irrCharsPrimeToDeg p G) : ∃ n : ℕ, χ 1 = n ∧ ¬ p ∣ n := by
  obtain ⟨V, -, rfl, hV⟩ := hχ
  exact ⟨Module.finrank ℂ V, FDRep.char_one V, hV⟩

/-- **McKay conjecture.** Let $G$ be a finite group, $p$ a prime and $P$ a Sylow $p$-subgroup
of $G$. Then the number of irreducible complex characters of $G$ of degree not divisible by $p$
equals the number of irreducible complex characters of the normalizer $N_G(P)$ of degree not
divisible by $p$:
$$|\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(G)| = |\mathrm{Irr}_{p'}(N_G(P))|.$$

Here isomorphic representations are counted once. Since all Sylow $p$-subgroups are conjugate,
the right-hand side does not depend on the choice of $P$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem mckay_conjecture (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (P : Sylow p G) :
    (irrCharsPrimeToDeg p G).ncard = (irrCharsPrimeToDeg p P.normalizer).ncard := by
  sorry

end McKayConjecture

items: Both sides count p'-degree irreducible characters, |Irr_{p'}(G)| = |Irr_{p'}(N_G(P))|, following the article's Statement section and Cabanes–Späth. The list entry's literal wording (all irreducible characters of N_G(P)) is false in general (e.g. G = S_3, p = 3) and is clearly a terse abbreviation.

"group" is read as finite group: `[Finite G]`. `p` is a prime via `[Fact p.Prime]`, and `P : Sylow p G` is an arbitrary Sylow p-subgroup; the normalizer is `P.normalizer = Subgroup.normalizer ↑P`, coerced to a type.

Irreducible complex representations are modelled as simple objects (`CategoryTheory.Simple`) of `FDRep ℂ G`, which is Mathlib's convention for irreducibility of finite-dimensional representations (used in `FDRep.char_orthonormal`, `FDRep.simple_iff_char_is_norm_one`). `FDRep ℂ G` is abelian, so `Simple` means nonzero with no proper nonzero subrepresentation.

Characters are taken as functions `G → ℂ` via `FDRep.character`; counting the set of characters counts each isomorphism class of irreducible representations once (isomorphic representations have equal characters, `FDRep.char_iso`), matching the article's 'we count isomorphic representations as the same'.

The degree of a character is `Module.finrank ℂ V`, equal to χ(1) by `FDRep.char_one`; the condition is `¬ p ∣ Module.finrank ℂ V` in ℕ (divisibility in ℂ would be vacuous). An API lemma records that each χ in the set has χ 1 = n for some n : ℕ with ¬ p ∣ n.

Cardinality is `Set.ncard`. For finite G the set of irreducible characters is finite (they are orthonormal in the finite-dimensional space of functions G → ℂ), so the default value 0 on infinite sets is never reached.
`G : Type` (universe 0) because `FDRep (R G : Type u)` forces `G` to live in the universe of `ℂ`. Every finite group is isomorphic to one in `Type`, so this is not a mathematical restriction.

Category tag is `research open` to match the status given in the task, although the conjecture is now a theorem (Cabanes–Späth, arXiv:2410.20392); the module docstring mentions the announced proof. A reviewer may prefer `research solved`.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity in the source: the list entry drops 'of degree not divisible by p' on the normalizer side; following the decomposition notes, the article's Statement section and Cabanes–Späth (MK), both sides are restricted to p'-degree characters (the literal reading is false in general). Status: the file is tagged `research open` to match the given status label and the source list, but the conjecture is now a theorem (Cabanes–Späth, arXiv:2410.20392, 2024); a maintainer may prefer `@[category research solved]` (the repository's formal_proof attribute has no 'informal' kind, so only the category tag would change). G is taken in `Type` because `FDRep ℂ G` forces G into the universe of ℂ; every finite group is isomorphic to one in `Type`, so no generality is lost. The bespoke definition `irrCharsPrimeToDeg` is kept in the problem file; it could reasonably be promoted to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as a general Irr(G) definition. Set.ncard is used (repository-idiomatic); finiteness of the set of irreducible characters is a theorem (orthonormality), so no junk value is reachable; encard/Cardinal.mk (c04, c05, c07) would be equally faithful.
